task_instance: Build the SKILL.md 'Core Workflow: aiohttp-hosted AgentApplication' sample as a runnable local agent: install the microsoft-agents-* Python packages, wire up MemoryStorage + MsalConnectionManager + CloudAdapter + Authorization + AgentApplication behind aiohttp, register a membersAdded welcome handler, a '/status' command handler, and a generic message echo handler, run it as a local server on /api/messages, and drive it with synthetic Bot Framework Activity JSON payloads to verify routing and replies actually work.
evidence: Installed microsoft-agents-hosting-core, microsoft-agents-hosting-aiohttp, microsoft-agents-activity, microsoft-agents-authentication-msal, microsoft-agents-copilotstudio-client (v1.7.0) via pip; all imports in the SKILL.md sample resolved (AgentApplication, TurnState, TurnContext, MemoryStorage, Authorization, CloudAdapter, start_agent_process, jwt_authorization_middleware, MsalConnectionManager, load_configuration_from_env). Wrote app.py implementing the documented Core Workflow verbatim plus the AgentApplication routing handlers (membersAdded welcome, '/status' string route, generic 'message' echo route) and .env with ANONYMOUS_ALLOWED=True (no real Azure/Bot credentials used, since account-bound services are off-limits). Ran `python3 app.py`, which started aiohttp on localhost:3978 and logged the SDK's own connection/config diagnostics. Because a real Bot Framework Connector/Azure Bot Service channel is an external account-bound service (out of scope per safety rules), I added a small local stand-in route in the same aiohttp app for POST /v3/conversations/{id}/activities (the Connector API the adapter calls to deliver replies) purely to observe the SDK's own outbound reply payloads locally; it performs no real network egress. Sent synthetic Activity JSON via curl to POST /api/messages for three cases: a 'hello' message, a '/status' message, and a conversationUpdate with membersAdded. All three returned HTTP 202 from the SDK's start_agent_process/CloudAdapter pipeline, and the SDK's own reply activities were captured in sent_replies.jsonl: {"text": "You said: hello", "replyToId": "1"}, {"text": "Status: OK", "replyToId": "2"}, {"text": "Welcome to the agent!", "replyToId": "3"} -- confirming AgentApplication's decorator-based routing (conversation_update('membersAdded'), message('/status'), activity('message')), TurnContext.send_activity, and the full aiohttp hosting/adapter pipeline all function as documented.
